DATA PREPROCESSING & CLEANING

# Remove missing values
penguins_clean <- na.omit(penguins) # Rows with missing values were removed to ensure model consistency

# Convert character data types to factor
# Categorical variables were converted to factors for proper handling in modeling
penguins_clean$species <- as.factor(penguins_clean$species)
penguins_clean$island <- as.factor(penguins_clean$island)
penguins_clean$sex <- as.factor(penguins_clean$sex)

# Feature Selection / Relationship Analysis
numeric_data <- penguins_clean[, sapply(penguins_clean, is.numeric)]
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data)
cor_matrix
##                   culmen_length_mm culmen_depth_mm flipper_length_mm
## culmen_length_mm         1.0000000      -0.2286400         0.6521257
## culmen_depth_mm         -0.2286400       1.0000000        -0.5787295
## flipper_length_mm        0.6521257      -0.5787295         1.0000000
## body_mass_g              0.5890662      -0.4729870         0.8732110
##                   body_mass_g
## culmen_length_mm    0.5890662
## culmen_depth_mm    -0.4729870
## flipper_length_mm   0.8732110
## body_mass_g         1.0000000
heatmap(
  cor_matrix,
  main = "Correlation Heatmap",
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50))

library(corrplot)
## Warning: package 'corrplot' was built under R version 4.4.3
## corrplot 0.95 loaded
corrplot(
  cor_matrix,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200),
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.srt = 45,
  addCoef.col = "black")

# The heatmap reveals moderate to strong correlations among certain predictors, suggesting potential multicollinearity. 
# However, no correlations exceeded a critical threshold (e.g., 0.9), so all variables were retained. 

# Scatterplot Matrix
pairs(
  penguins_clean[, c(
    "culmen_length_mm",
    "culmen_depth_mm",
    "flipper_length_mm",
    "body_mass_g"
  )],
  col = penguins_clean$species,
  pch = 19,
  main = "Scatterplot Matrix")

# Train/Test Data Split
set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(1:nrow(penguins_clean), 0.7 * nrow(penguins_clean))

train_data_original <- penguins_clean[train_index, ]
test_data_original  <- penguins_clean[-train_index, ]

train_data <- penguins_clean[train_index, ] # for normalized versions
test_data  <- penguins_clean[-train_index, ]

# Normalize Numerical Variables (for NN, KNN, SVM)
numeric_cols <- sapply(train_data, is.numeric) # identify numeric columns
normalize <- function(x) {
  (x - min(x)) / (max(x) - min(x))}

train_data[, numeric_cols] <- lapply(train_data[, numeric_cols], normalize)
test_data[, numeric_cols]  <- lapply(test_data[, numeric_cols], normalize)

# Dummy Variable Encoding (for NN, KNN, SVM)
train_encoded <- data.frame(model.matrix(species ~ . -1, data = train_data))
test_encoded  <- data.frame(model.matrix(species ~ . -1, data = test_data))
train_encoded$species <- train_data$species
test_encoded$species  <- test_data$species

# PCA (principal component analysis)
# PCA was explored as a dimensionality reduction technique. 
# However, because the dataset contained relatively few predictors and no extremely high correlations among numerical variables, 
# dimensionality reduction was ultimately not necessary for improving model performance.
penguins_numeric <- penguins_clean[, c(
  "culmen_length_mm",
  "culmen_depth_mm",
  "flipper_length_mm",
  "body_mass_g")]

pca_model <- prcomp(
  penguins_numeric,
  scale. = TRUE)

summary(pca_model)
## Importance of components:
##                           PC1    PC2     PC3     PC4
## Standard deviation     1.6570 0.8820 0.60714 0.32829
## Proportion of Variance 0.6864 0.1945 0.09216 0.02694
## Cumulative Proportion  0.6864 0.8809 0.97306 1.00000
pca_data <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_model$x[,1],
  PC2 = pca_model$x[,2],
  species = penguins_clean$species)

var_explained <- round(
  100 * summary(pca_model)$importance[2, 1:2],
  1)

plot(
  pca_data$PC1,
  pca_data$PC2,
  col = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen")[
    as.numeric(pca_data$species)
  ],
  pch = 19,
  xlab = paste0(
    "PC1 (",
    var_explained[1],
    "% Variance)"
  ),
  ylab = paste0(
    "PC2 (",
    var_explained[2],
    "% Variance)"
  ),
  main = "PCA Projection of Penguins Dataset")

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = levels(pca_data$species),
  col = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen"),
  pch = 19,
  bty = "o",
  bg = "white")

ALGORITHM 1 - DECISION TREE

# MODEL 1 - DECISION TREE
# Using ctree
library(party)

## Loading required package: grid

## 
##     as.Date, as.Date.numeric

## 
## Attaching package: 'party'
## The following object is masked from 'package:dplyr':
## 
##     where
penguins_ctree <- ctree(species ~ culmen_length_mm + culmen_depth_mm +
                          flipper_length_mm + body_mass_g + island + sex,
                        data = train_data_original)
penguins_ctree
## 
##   Conditional inference tree with 5 terminal nodes
## 
## Response:  species 
## Inputs:  culmen_length_mm, culmen_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, island, sex 
## Number of observations:  233 
## 
## 1) island == {Dream, Torgersen}; criterion = 1, statistic = 197.207
##   2) culmen_length_mm <= 42.2; criterion = 1, statistic = 88.49
##     3)*  weights = 68 
##   2) culmen_length_mm > 42.2
##     4) culmen_length_mm <= 44.1; criterion = 0.995, statistic = 29.351
##       5)*  weights = 10 
##     4) culmen_length_mm > 44.1
##       6)*  weights = 42 
## 1) island == {Biscoe}
##   7) flipper_length_mm <= 200; criterion = 1, statistic = 87.709
##     8)*  weights = 30 
##   7) flipper_length_mm > 200
##     9)*  weights = 83
plot(penguins_ctree)

plot(penguins_ctree, type = "simple")

# Predict on training data
trainPred_ctree <- predict(penguins_ctree, train_data_original)
train_conf_matrix_ctree <- table(trainPred_ctree, train_data_original$species)
train_conf_matrix_ctree
##                
## trainPred_ctree Adelie Chinstrap Gentoo
##       Adelie       102         6      0
##       Chinstrap      0        42      0
##       Gentoo         0         0     83
train_accuracy_ctree <- sum(diag(train_conf_matrix_ctree)) / sum(train_conf_matrix_ctree)
train_accuracy_ctree
## [1] 0.9742489
# Predict on test data
testPred_ctree <- predict(penguins_ctree, test_data_original)
test_conf_matrix_ctree <- table(testPred_ctree, test_data_original$species)
test_conf_matrix_ctree
##               
## testPred_ctree Adelie Chinstrap Gentoo
##      Adelie        41         0      0
##      Chinstrap      2        20      0
##      Gentoo         1         0     37
test_accuracy_ctree <- sum(diag(test_conf_matrix_ctree)) / sum(test_conf_matrix_ctree)
test_accuracy_ctree
## [1] 0.970297
# Using rpart
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
## Warning: package 'rpart.plot' was built under R version 4.4.3
dt_model <- rpart(species ~ culmen_length_mm + culmen_depth_mm +
                    flipper_length_mm + body_mass_g + island + sex,
                  data = train_data_original)
print(dt_model)
## n= 233 
## 
## node), split, n, loss, yval, (yprob)
##       * denotes terminal node
## 
## 1) root 233 131 Adelie (0.43776824 0.20600858 0.35622318)  
##   2) flipper_length_mm< 206.5 145  44 Adelie (0.69655172 0.30344828 0.00000000)  
##     4) culmen_length_mm< 44.65 106   6 Adelie (0.94339623 0.05660377 0.00000000) *
##     5) culmen_length_mm>=44.65 39   1 Chinstrap (0.02564103 0.97435897 0.00000000) *
##   3) flipper_length_mm>=206.5 88   5 Gentoo (0.01136364 0.04545455 0.94318182)  
##     6) culmen_depth_mm>=17.05 7   3 Chinstrap (0.14285714 0.57142857 0.28571429) *
##     7) culmen_depth_mm< 17.05 81   0 Gentoo (0.00000000 0.00000000 1.00000000) *
rpart.plot(dt_model,
           type = 2,
           extra = 104,
           fallen.leaves = TRUE)

# Predict on training data
trainPred_dt <- predict(dt_model, train_data_original, type = 'class')
train_conf_matrix_dt <- table(trainPred_dt, train_data_original$species)
train_conf_matrix_dt
##             
## trainPred_dt Adelie Chinstrap Gentoo
##    Adelie       100         6      0
##    Chinstrap      2        42      2
##    Gentoo         0         0     81
train_accuracy_dt <- sum(diag(train_conf_matrix_dt)) / sum(train_conf_matrix_dt)
train_accuracy_dt
## [1] 0.9570815
# Predict on test data
testPred_dt <- predict(dt_model, test_data_original, type = "class")
test_conf_matrix_dt <- table(Predicted = testPred_dt, Actual = test_data_original$species)
test_conf_matrix_dt
##            Actual
## Predicted   Adelie Chinstrap Gentoo
##   Adelie        41         0      0
##   Chinstrap      3        20      2
##   Gentoo         0         0     35
test_accuracy_dt <- sum(diag(test_conf_matrix_dt)) / sum(test_conf_matrix_dt)
test_accuracy_dt
## [1] 0.950495
# Selecting the best tree (rpart)
printcp(dt_model) # CP is complexity parameter, xerror is cross-validated error which should be minimized.
## 
## Classification tree:
## rpart(formula = species ~ culmen_length_mm + culmen_depth_mm + 
##     flipper_length_mm + body_mass_g + island + sex, data = train_data_original)
## 
## Variables actually used in tree construction:
## [1] culmen_depth_mm   culmen_length_mm  flipper_length_mm
## 
## Root node error: 131/233 = 0.56223
## 
## n= 233 
## 
##         CP nsplit rel error  xerror     xstd
## 1 0.625954      0  1.000000 1.00000 0.057808
## 2 0.282443      1  0.374046 0.38168 0.047837
## 3 0.015267      2  0.091603 0.12977 0.030304
## 4 0.010000      3  0.076336 0.12214 0.029467
plotcp(dt_model)

opt <- which.min(dt_model$cptable[, "xerror"]) # select optimal CP
cp  <- dt_model$cptable[opt, "CP"]
pruned_model <- prune(dt_model, cp = cp)
pruned_model
## n= 233 
## 
## node), split, n, loss, yval, (yprob)
##       * denotes terminal node
## 
## 1) root 233 131 Adelie (0.43776824 0.20600858 0.35622318)  
##   2) flipper_length_mm< 206.5 145  44 Adelie (0.69655172 0.30344828 0.00000000)  
##     4) culmen_length_mm< 44.65 106   6 Adelie (0.94339623 0.05660377 0.00000000) *
##     5) culmen_length_mm>=44.65 39   1 Chinstrap (0.02564103 0.97435897 0.00000000) *
##   3) flipper_length_mm>=206.5 88   5 Gentoo (0.01136364 0.04545455 0.94318182)

# Partial NN Model
# Select only numeric predictors + target from pre-processed data (which has already been normalized, no encoding needed because we are selecting two numeric predictors). For the partial NN, KNN, and SVM models, we will focus on culmen depth and culmen length as our predictors because are biologically meaningful and separate species relatively well.
train_scaled_nn <- train_data[, c(
  "culmen_length_mm",

  "culmen_depth_mm",
  "species")]

# Train Neural Network
nn_model <- nnet(
  species ~ .,
  data = train_scaled_nn,
  size = 5,
  maxit = 300,
  trace = FALSE)

# Predictions and Evaluation
pred_class_nn <- predict(nn_model, test_scaled_nn, type = "class")
conf_mat_nn <- table(Predicted = pred_class_nn, Actual = test_scaled_nn$species)

## [1] 0.8514851
# Create Decision Region Grid
x_seq <- seq(min(train_scaled_nn$culmen_length_mm) - 0.5,
             max(train_scaled_nn$culmen_length_mm) + 0.5,
             length.out = 200)

             max(train_scaled_nn$culmen_depth_mm) + 0.5,
             length.out = 200)

grid <- expand.grid(

grid_matrix <- matrix(
  as.numeric(grid_pred),
  nrow = length(x_seq),
  ncol = length(y_seq))

accuracy_results_knn <- data.frame(
  k = integer(),
  accuracy = numeric())

for(i in k_values){
  pred_knn <- knn(
    train = train_scaled_knn[, 1:2],
    test  = test_scaled_knn[, 1:2],

  )
  
  acc_knn <- mean(
    pred_knn ==

  )
  
  accuracy_results_knn <- rbind(
    accuracy_results_knn,
    data.frame(
      k = i,
      accuracy = acc_knn
    )
  )

# Check clustering result against Species label
table(penguins_clean$species, kmeans_result$cluster)
##            
##               1   2   3
##   Adelie      0  22 124
##   Chinstrap   0  63   5
##   Gentoo    120   0   0
# Class Gentoo can easily be separated from other clusters, classes Adelie and Chinstrap are to a small degree overlapped with each other

# Plot for Culmen Length and Culmen Depth
plot(
  penguins_kmeans_scaled[, c("culmen_length_mm", "culmen_depth_mm")],
  col = kmeans_result$cluster,
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Culmen Length",
  ylab = "Culmen Depth",
  main = "K-Means Clustering (Penguins)")

points(
  kmeans_result$centers[, c("culmen_length_mm", "culmen_depth_mm")],
  col = 1:3,
  pch = 8,
  cex = 2)

# Alternate Plot for Culmen Length and Flipper Length
plot(
  penguins_kmeans_scaled[, c("culmen_length_mm", "flipper_length_mm")],
  col = kmeans_result$cluster,
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Culmen Length",
  ylab = "Flipper Length",
  main = "K-Means Clustering (Penguins)")

points(
  kmeans_result$centers[, c("culmen_length_mm", "flipper_length_mm")],
  col = 1:3,
  pch = 8,
  cex = 2)

# Alternate Plot for Body Mass and Flipper Length
plot(
  penguins_kmeans_scaled[, c("body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm")],
  col = kmeans_result$cluster,
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Body Mass",
  ylab = "Flipper Length",
  main = "K-Means Clustering (Penguins)")

points(
  kmeans_result$centers[, c("body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm")],
  col = 1:3,
  pch = 8,
  cex = 2)

# Test predictions, confusion matrix, and accuracy
test_pred_ada <- predict.boosting(
  penguins_ada,
  newdata = test_data_original)

test_conf_ada <- table(
  Predicted = test_pred_ada$class,
  Actual = test_data_original$species)
test_conf_ada
##            Actual
## Predicted   Adelie Chinstrap Gentoo
##   Adelie        42         0      0
##   Chinstrap      2        20      0
##   Gentoo         0         0     37
test_acc_ada <- mean(
  test_pred_ada$class ==
    test_data_original$species)
test_acc_ada
## [1] 0.980198
# Variable Importance
importanceplot(penguins_ada)

ALGORITHM EVALUATION AND COMPARISON

model_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Decision Tree (ctree)",
    "Decision Tree (rpart)",
    "Random Forest",
    "Naive Bayes Partial",
    "Naive Bayes Full",
    "Neural Network Partial",
    "Neural Network Full",
    "KNN Partial",
    "KNN Full",
    "SVM Partial",
    "SVM Full",
    "AdaBoost",
    "K-Means"
  ),
  
  Accuracy = c(
    test_accuracy_ctree,
    test_accuracy_dt,
    accuracy_rf,
    nb_accuracy,
    nb_full_accuracy,
    accuracy_nn,
    accuracy_nn_full,
    knn_accuracy,
    knn_accuracy_full,
    svm_accuracy,
    svm_accuracy_full,
    test_acc_ada,
    NA
  )
)

model_results
##                     Model  Accuracy
## 1   Decision Tree (ctree) 0.9702970
## 2   Decision Tree (rpart) 0.9504950
## 3           Random Forest 1.0000000
## 4     Naive Bayes Partial 0.9207921
## 5        Naive Bayes Full 1.0000000
## 6  Neural Network Partial 0.8514851
## 7     Neural Network Full 0.8514851
## 8             KNN Partial 0.8712871
## 9                KNN Full 0.9900990
## 10            SVM Partial 0.8712871
## 11               SVM Full 0.9603960
## 12               AdaBoost 0.9801980
## 13                K-Means        NA
barplot(
  model_results$Accuracy,
  names.arg = model_results$Model,
  las = 2,
  main = "Comparison of Classification Model Accuracy",
  ylab = "Accuracy",
  ylim = c(0,1))

library(pheatmap)
## Warning: package 'pheatmap' was built under R version 4.4.3
# Set row names
rownames(model_results) <- model_results$Model
# Remove model column
model_results$Model <- NULL
# Convert to numeric matrix
accuracy_matrix <- as.matrix(model_results)
# Accuracy Heatmap
pheatmap(
  accuracy_matrix,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  display_numbers = TRUE,
  number_format = "%.3f",
  color = colorRampPalette(
    c("white", "cadetblue1", "cadetblue4")
  )(100),
  main = "Model Accuracy Comparison")
